claims.text: Earlier, in FOI-1730-1819 (published 22 October 2018), TfL reported elevated rail roughness between 720 and 880m on the Central line between Bethnal Green and Mile End and stated it would undertake rail grinding at that location in February 2019.

citations.quote: We will undertake rail grinding at this location in February 2019, with the intention to improve the wheel-rail interface.

claims.text: In FOI-1231-2425, TfL disclosed in-cab noise measurements taken on Monday 24 June 2024 on the Central line, recording 87 dB LAeq eastbound and 86 dB LAeq westbound between Liverpool Street and Bethnal Green, and 83 dB LAeq eastbound and 82 dB LAeq westbound between Bethnal Green and Mile End, with readings carried out on a bi-monthly period.

citations.quote: June 2024, these measurements were taken from within the train operator's cab.

Bethnal Green to Mile End | 83
Mile End to Bethnal Green | 82
Bethnal Green to Liverpool Street | 86
Readings are carried out on a bi-monthly period.

claims.text: In TfL's 24 June 2024 in-cab dataset (FOI-1231-2425), Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green was 4 dB LAeq higher than Bethnal Green to Mile End in both the eastbound (87 vs 83 dB LAeq) and westbound (86 vs 82 dB LAeq) directions.

citations.quote: Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green | 87

claims.text: For workplace noise assessments under The Control of Noise at Work Regulations 2005, TfL references a lower exposure action value of 80 dB(A), an upper exposure action value of 85 dB(A), and an exposure limit value of 87 dB(A) for daily personal noise exposure.

citations.quote: The noise data was analysed with respect to The Control of Noise at Work Regulations 2005 (CNAWR), specifically:
the 'lower exposure action value', corresponding to a daily personal noise exposure level of 80 dB(A);
the 'upper exposure action value', corresponding to a daily personal noise exposure level of 85 dB(A);
and the 'exposure limit value', corresponding to a daily personal noise exposure level of 87 dB(A).

claims.text: In our uncalibrated relative phone-audio recordings, mean relative levels were -18.66 dBFS(A) on eastbound LST-BTH (n=6) and -19.42 dBFS(A) on eastbound BTH-MLE (n=6), while westbound levels were -18.8 dBFS(A) on BTH-LST (n=5) and -19.07 dBFS(A) on MLE-BTH (n=5).

Within-trip comparisons across 11 trips show LST-BTH was louder than BTH-MLE in 10 of 11 trips with a mean relative difference of 0.54 dB (range -0.13 to 1.21 dB), resulting in a pre-registered NO-GO verdict because the difference is below 1 dB and inside phone limiter compression and run-to-run variation.

In our uncalibrated relative dBFS(A) measurements, eastbound LST-BTH (-18.66 dBFS(A)) was 6.86 dB higher than the sub-surface Hammersmith & City and Circle line section between Aldgate East and Whitechapel (-25.52 dBFS(A)).

Indicative whole-trip passenger-saloon measurements using the NIOSH sound level meter app recorded 91.9 dB(A) LAeq eastbound from Liverpool Street to Mile End (n=1) and 87.3 dB(A) LAeq westbound from Mile End to Liverpool Street (n=1), including platform and dwell time, though the app is validated only up to about 85 dB(A) so readings may read low and cannot be compared like-for-like with TfL's per-section in-cab figures.

At Mayor's Question Time on 16 July 2026 (Question 2026/2156), Elly Baker AM stated that TfL's Government Relations team sent an email turning down the majority of her requests for Tube noise data, and the Mayor promised to ensure TfL provides far more detailed information including six-month rail grinding activity and track renewal programmes.

citations.quote: just an email from TfL's Government Relations turning down the majority of the requests for data.

I will make sure it provides, in addition, information on what in real-time rail grinding activity is taking place over the next six months, the track renewal programmes, alternative noise reduction measures that are being considered or in delivery.

claims.text: A secondary press article in Brixton Buzz (27 January 2026, attributing the information to JRPass) cites 92.8 decibels for Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green, but the underlying TfL dataset, measurement date, direction, and car location for that figure are not in the primary corpus.

citations.quote: Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green (Central line) – 92.8 decibels
Daniel de Nieuwe, Head of Product from JRPass said:

claims.text: Because Mayor's Question 2022/1791 does not specify whether one or both track directions were ground between December 2021 and May 2022, and because no post-2022 Central line grinding logs or post-June 2024 bi-monthly in-cab logs are in the public corpus, the public record cannot establish when LST-BTH and BTH-MLE were last ground or whether planned eastbound deep Tube reconditioning on LST-BTH was completed.

asks.request: Provide all bi-monthly Central line in-cab noise measurement tables (LAeq and LCpeak by inter-station section and direction) recorded from January 2022 to the present, specifically including Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green and Bethnal Green to Mile End.
asks.why: TfL confirmed in FOI-1231-2425 that Central line in-cab readings are carried out bi-monthly, yet only the single snapshot from 24 June 2024 is available in the public record (C05, C06, C14).

asks.request: Provide the complete log of rail grinding works (dates, direction/road, and chainage/metres ground) and confirm the completion status and dates of the 2023/24 planned Deep Tube Reconditioning works between Liverpool Street, Bethnal Green, and Mile End from December 2021 to the present.
asks.why: MQ 2022/1791 and the December 2022 Head of Track letter show grinding took place in Dec 2021-May 2022 and DTR was planned for 2023/24 on LST-BTH Eastbound, but do not specify which track directions were ground or whether further grinding or DTR was completed despite TfL noting grinding usually needs repeating every 6 to 12 months (C01, C03, C04, C14).

asks.request: Identify the specific TfL disclosure or dataset that contained the 92.8 dB figure for Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green cited by JRPass and Brixton Buzz, including the measurement date, car/cab location, and metric definition.
asks.why: Resolves the provenance gap between the secondary press report of 92.8 dB and TfL's primary 24 June 2024 in-cab figures of 87 dB eastbound and 86 dB westbound (C05, C13).

asks.request: Disclose the rail roughness / corrugation plots and any passenger-saloon acoustic measurements held by TfL for Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green and Bethnal Green to Mile End since 2021.
asks.why: TfL previously released rail roughness plots for BTH-MLE in FOI-1730-1819 and claims a data-led approach to corrugation, while our indicative passenger-saloon readings and relative audio recordings cannot directly measure rail corrugation or substitute for calibrated saloon and track data (C02, C08, C09, C11, C12).
